facts: After leaving the main path and descending into a wet field, Udayaditya's horse, Sugriva, falls onto its front legs three times.
Basanta Ray plays an alap in Raga Vehag before singing the line "Keyse katongi rayan, so piya bina".
The Mahishi forces Vibha to wear eight thick gold bangles on each arm.
The Mahishi forces Vibha to wear one huge diamond bracelet on each arm.
The canal is seventy cubits below the Jessore palace roof.
The sheet-rope is tied to a small pillar.
Hanumanprasad Tewari is the palace guard who is dozing off on watch when Sitaram punches him in the back as a "joke".
The eight-year-old Samaraditya breaks five strings of Basanta Ray's instrument.
The eight-year-old Samaraditya snatches away the mezrab (plectrum) of Basanta Ray's instrument.
After finishing his burglary, the thief asks the husband to give him a pipeful of tobacco.
Mangala brings out a dried root and gives it to the maidservant Matangini to feed to Matangini's husband with his paan.
Vibha brings a parakeet to hang in Udayaditya's prison cell to make it more comfortable.
Sitaram throws some bones into the burning prison cell to fake Udayaditya's death.
Sitaram throws a skull into the burning prison cell to fake Udayaditya's death.
Sitaram throws Udayaditya's sword into the burning prison cell to fake Udayaditya's death.
Udayaditya was given responsibility for the Hosenkhali pargana at age sixteen to teach him the work of ruling.
Ramai Thakur calls the Mahishi "Mother Nikasha" right before Rammohan recognizes Ramai Thakur.
The two inexperienced people who fail to stand up for Ramchandra Ray's palanquin are weavers.
Bhagavat paid off the loans he accumulated during his hard times by selling his pots and pans.
On the veranda in Raigarh, as the sun is setting, Basanta Ray enthusiastically requests Khan Saheb to sing "Tajbe Taj Naube Nau."
During his argument with the minister about dharma, Pratapaditya cites Bhrigu as the mythological figure who killed Bhrigu's mother at Bhrigu's father's request.
Mangala spends five days performing tasks like cutting, soaking, grinding, mixing, and chanting mantras to prepare the poison meant for Surma.
Ramai Bhand suggests sending a couple of green bananas to Pratapaditya's daughter alongside a platter of sweets.
Udayaditya states that he wants to establish a guest house with the requested money.
Udayaditya states that he wants to establish a temple with the requested money.
Rammohan threatens to have Ramai Bhand's head shaved.
Rammohan threatens to pour whey over Ramai Bhand's head.
Pratapaditya accuses the minister of losing a letter.
Pratapaditya accuses the minister of sending a man to Umesh Ray instead of going there himself.
Udayaditya uses Udayaditya's own cloth to tie up Sitaram.
Sitaram's sister realizes that giving her child a lowly job would insult her brother Sitaram's honor.
After Rammohan explicitly refuses to deliver the letter of renunciation to Jessore, King Ramchandra Ray hands the letter to the old Nayanchand instead.
Udayaditya screams, "Grand-uncle, beware!"
On the night of Ramchandra Ray's escape, Udayaditya subdues Sitaram.
On the night of Ramchandra Ray's escape, Udayaditya ties up Sitaram to bypass Sitaram and facilitate Ramchandra Ray's escape.
On the night of Udayaditya's own escape from prison, Sitaram orchestrates Udayaditya's escape.
Sitaram stages a fire to facilitate Udayaditya's escape.
Sitaram leads Udayaditya out of Udayaditya's cell.
Pratapaditya initially sends two Pathans to intercept Basanta Ray at an inn in Simultali.
The two Pathans are sent to kill Basanta Ray.
The initial assassination plan fails when the assassin seeks refuge instead.
Muktiyar Khan is Pratapaditya's commander.
Pratapaditya finally sends Muktiyar Khan directly to Raigarh with written orders.
Abdul executes Basanta Ray with a sword at Raigarh.
Abdul's execution of Basanta Ray fulfills Pratapaditya's plan to end the old king's life.
Rammohan Mal first beats Ramai Bhand in the Jessore inner quarters.
Ramai Bhand is disguised as a middle-aged woman during the encounter in the Jessore inner quarters.
Ramai Bhand uses the middle-aged woman disguise to mock the Mahishi.
Rammohan Mal later throws Ramai Bhand out of the king's room in the Chandradwip palace.
Ramai Bhand appears undisguised as the court jester during the encounter in the king's room.
Ramai Bhand makes a crude remark about Vibha in the king's room.
Rammohan Mal throws Ramai Bhand out of the king's room in retaliation for the crude remark about Vibha.
Surma dies after consuming poison.
The sorceress Mangala (Rukmini) prepared the poison Surma consumed.
Matangini was the Mahishi's maid.
Matangini secretly contracted Mangala (Rukmini).
Matangini contracted Mangala (Rukmini) to turn Udayaditya's affections away from Udayaditya's wife, Surma.
Udayaditya is Vibha's brother.
Udayaditya is grieving.
Vibha refuses to leave Udayaditya because Udayaditya is grieving.
Ramchandra Ray feels insulted by Vibha's refusal.
Because of Vibha's refusal, Ramchandra Ray decides to marry another woman out of spite.
Vibha eventually travels to Chandradwip.
Vibha arrives in Chandradwip on the day of Ramchandra Ray's new wedding.
Vibha is rejected when Vibha arrives in Chandradwip.
Udayaditya gives his signet ring to Rukmini to get Rukmini to leave Udayaditya's dark room.
Sitaram and Bhagavat are guards.
Sitaram and Bhagavat use the seal from Udayaditya's ring to stamp a forged petition.
The forged petition is addressed to the Emperor of Delhi.
The forged petition is written as though from Udayaditya.
The forged petition accuses Pratapaditya of rebelling against the Emperor of Delhi.
The forged petition asks that the kingdom be given to Udayaditya instead of Pratapaditya.
Bhagavat delivers the forged petition straight to Pratapaditya.
Bhagavat claims to have intercepted the forged petition before it could reach Delhi.
Bhagavat delivers the forged petition to Pratapaditya to get Bhagavat's palace job back.
During Ramchandra's escape, Udayaditya overpowers the guard Sitaram.
During Ramchandra's escape, Udayaditya overpowers the guard Bhagavat.
Sitaram is dismissed as a consequence of Ramchandra's escape.
Bhagavat is dismissed as a consequence of Ramchandra's escape.
Sitaram falls into poverty after Sitaram's dismissal.
Bhagavat falls into poverty after Bhagavat's dismissal.
Udayaditya and Surma secretly provide Sitaram a monthly stipend.
Udayaditya and Surma secretly provide Bhagavat a monthly stipend.
Udayaditya and Surma provide the stipends out of guilt.
Pratapaditya learns of Udayaditya and Surma's defiance in providing the stipends.
Pratapaditya retaliates against this defiance by ordering Surma to leave the palace.
The song 'I alone am left behind' represents Basanta Ray's profound loneliness.
The song 'I alone am left behind' represents Basanta Ray's grief over losing his loved ones.
Basanta Ray first sings 'I alone am left behind' alone in Raigarh.
Basanta Ray watches the sunset while first singing 'I alone am left behind' in Raigarh.
Basanta Ray feels isolated while first singing 'I alone am left behind' in Raigarh.
Basanta Ray later sings 'I alone am left behind' directly to Vibha in Jessore.
Basanta Ray's later singing of 'I alone am left behind' follows Basanta Ray's seeing Surma's empty room.
Basanta Ray's later singing of 'I alone am left behind' follows Basanta Ray's realization that Surma has died.
Rukmini's frantic attempt to board the escape boat fails.
Rukmini falls into the canal after failing to board the escape boat.
Rukmini is enraged after the failed attempt.
Rukmini goes to Pratapaditya's court after falling into the canal.
At Pratapaditya's court, Rukmini reveals that Basanta Ray orchestrated Udayaditya's escape.
Rukmini's revelation prompts King Pratapaditya to send assassins to Raigarh.
Pratapaditya greets Ramchandra with cold indifference.
Pratapaditya ignores Ramchandra to read a mundane tax document.
Pratapaditya then abruptly dismisses Ramchandra.
Ramchandra later allows his courtiers in Chandradwip to openly mock Pratapaditya's newly established royal lineage.
Ramchandra allows this mockery to avenge Pratapaditya's slight.
Ramchandra's courtiers gleefully compare Pratapaditya's ancestors to earthworms and leeches.
Rukmini is a widow.
Rukmini briefly infatuated the young Udayaditya in Raigarh.
Rukmini changes her name to Mangala.
Rukmini moves to the outskirts of Jessore.
Rukmini's jealousy leads Rukmini to brew poison.
Surma is Udayaditya's wife.
The poison brewed by Rukmini kills Surma.
After Surma's death, Rukmini sneaks into Udayaditya's room.
Rukmini demands Udayaditya's affection.
In early conversations with Surma, Udayaditya laments his birthright.
In early conversations with Surma, Udayaditya laments his father's belief that Udayaditya is unfit to rule.
Basanta Ray is executed.
Basanta Ray's execution traumatizes Udayaditya.
After the trauma of Basanta Ray's execution, Udayaditya formally swears an oath before Ma-Kali that Udayaditya will never touch the throne of Jessore.
Udayaditya designates Samaraditya as the rightful heir to the throne of Jessore.
Samaraditya is Udayaditya's younger brother.
Ramchandra sends a letter formally renouncing Vibha.
The messenger Nayanchand is frightened.
Nayanchand gives Ramchandra's letter to the Mahishi instead of the King.
Basanta Ray advises the Mahishi to hide the letter's true contents and tell Vibha that Ramchandra has affectionately sent for her.
Following Basanta Ray's advice, the Mahishi hides the letter's true contents.
The Mahishi tells Vibha that Ramchandra has affectionately sent for Vibha.
The Mahishi's misrepresentation causes Vibha to travel to Chandradwip under the tragic illusion that Ramchandra has affectionately sent for Vibha.
Pratapaditya orders the guards to block the canal adjoining the royal palace with large Sal wood logs.
Ramchandra's boat reaches the blockade.
Rammohan and his followers use their immense strength to pull Ramchandra's boat up and over the logs.
While Rammohan and his followers pull Ramchandra's boat over the logs, the guards are distracted trying to find weapons and a pursuit boat.
Initially, Basanta Ray is inseparable from his sitar.
Pratapaditya forces Basanta Ray away from Jessore.
Basanta Ray leaves his sitar behind in Jessore when Pratapaditya forces Basanta Ray away.
Basanta Ray vows not to play anymore.
Later, in Raigarh, Khan Saheb asks Basanta Ray to play.
Basanta Ray sadly admits to Khan Saheb that the sitar is there in Raigarh.
Basanta Ray says the sitar's strings are broken.
Basanta Ray says the sitar can no longer be tuned.
Initially, Udayaditya boldly involved himself in the subjects' affairs to protect the subjects.
Udayaditya's intervention on behalf of the subjects greatly annoyed Pratapaditya.
After Surma's death, Udayaditya was overwhelmed by a paralyzing fear of Udayaditya's father.
After Surma's death, Udayaditya retreated into Udayaditya's house instead of stopping an official from beating a tied-up subject.
Sitaram collaborates with Bhagavat to forge a treasonous petition.
The forged petition uses the Yubaraj's seal.
The forged petition leads directly to Udayaditya's imprisonment.
To undo Udayaditya's imprisonment, Sitaram orchestrates a fire diversion at the guardhouse.
Sitaram physically extracts Udayaditya from Udayaditya's cell.
Sitaram takes Udayaditya to a waiting escape boat.
In Jessore, Rammohan saves Ramchandra Ray from assassination.
Rammohan ties bedsheets into a rope to rescue Ramchandra Ray.
Rammohan lowers King Ramchandra Ray on Rammohan's back from the palace roof to a boat.
Later, in Chandradwip, Ramchandra Ray rejects Vibha.
Vibha faints after Ramchandra Ray rejects Vibha.
Rammohan physically lifts the unconscious Princess Vibha.
Rammohan carries Vibha out to a palanquin.
In Jessore, the Mahishi forces Vibha to wear heavy gold and diamond bangles.
In Jessore, the Mahishi forces Vibha to wear a large nose ring.
The Mahishi makes Vibha wear the jewelry to look suitably royal.
When Vibha travels to Chandradwip, Vibha sheds her royal status completely.
When Vibha travels to Chandradwip, Vibha refuses a palanquin.
When Vibha travels to Chandradwip, Vibha dresses as a commoner.
Vibha's commoner appearance leads Ramchandra to mistake Vibha for a beggar woman seeking alms.
After Surma's death, the bedchamber window is a place of grief for Udayaditya.
In his bedchamber, Udayaditya stares at the empty spot where Surma used to sit.
In his prison cell, the window (casement) becomes Udayaditya's only source of hope.
Udayaditya sleeps on the floor next to the prison-cell window so he can look at the sky and birds.
Udayaditya sleeps next to the prison-cell window so he can dream of freedom.
Initially, Sitaram flirts with Rukmini to borrow money from Rukmini.
Sitaram affectionately calls Rukmini 'Pranpriye.'
Sitaram does not intend to repay the money borrowed from Rukmini.
Sitaram verbally attacks Rukmini for getting Udayaditya imprisoned.
Sitaram's relationship with Rukmini collapses when Sitaram verbally attacks Rukmini.
Sitaram breaks into Rukmini's cottage to steal Rukmini's money.
Rukmini is traumatized when Sitaram breaks into Rukmini's cottage.
Sitaram's break-in prompts Rukmini to attack Sitaram with a curved blade.
Sitaram and his men initially start a fire near the guard huts.
The fire near the guard huts is intended to create a distraction.
The distraction allows Sitaram to open the prison door.
Sitaram sneaks Udayaditya out to a boat.
Later, Sitaram's men deliberately set Udayaditya's empty cell on fire.
Sitaram throws a melted sword into the flames.
Sitaram throws bones into the flames.
Sitaram throws the melted sword and bones into the flames to trick Pratapaditya into believing that Udayaditya perished.
Ramchandra Ray feels no gratitude toward Udayaditya for the rescue.
Ramchandra Ray regards the rescue as something that was bound to happen.
Ramchandra Ray assumes that everyone would unite to save Ramchandra Ray if Ramchandra Ray were in peril.
Ramchandra Ray tells himself that Udayaditya acted for the sake of Udayaditya's sister Vibha.
Ramchandra Ray believes that saving Ramchandra Ray's life was not Udayaditya's main objective.
The rescue is forgotten entirely in Ramchandra Ray's own court.
Ramchandra Ray brings up Udayaditya's name with the minister and Ramai Bhand in Ramchandra Ray's own court.
Ramchandra Ray, the minister, and Ramai Bhand laugh and joke about Udayaditya without a care.
Udayaditya is mocked for being Pratapaditya's son.
Pratapaditya's minister warns that executing Basanta Ray will anger the Emperor of Delhi.
Pratapaditya's minister warns that executing Basanta Ray will anger the Emperor of Delhi's fifty thousand soldiers.
Pratapaditya angrily rejects the minister's warnings.
Sitaram is a disgruntled guard.
Bhagavat is a disgruntled guard.
Sitaram and Bhagavat forge a petition to the Emperor of Delhi.
Sitaram and Bhagavat forge the petition in Udayaditya's name.
The forged petition claims treason.
Sitaram and Bhagavat successfully exploit Pratapaditya's paranoia through the forged petition.
The forged petition convinces Pratapaditya to imprison Udayaditya.
Udayaditya is Pratapaditya's son.
While alive, Surma acts as a loving confidant to Vibha.
The Mahishi ruins Vibha's hair with heavy styling.
After the Mahishi ruins Vibha's hair, Surma restyles it to Vibha's liking.
Surma dies by suicide.
Vibha grieves following Surma's suicide.
Following Surma's suicide, Vibha sits with unbraided hair.
Vibha endlessly waits for Surma to come fix Vibha's hair.
Rammohan later points to Vibha's unkempt hair as proof that Vibha is being neglected.
